Basic Information

  • Project Title: Applying Climate-Resilient Biogas Upgrade Approaches for Biohydrogen and Biomethane Recovery from Organic Wastes
  • Host Institution: University of Leeds
  • School/Faculty: School of Civil Engineering
  • Disciplines: Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 at 05:00 UTC+5
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded (EPSRC)
  • Eligibility: UK Only
  • Location: Leeds, United Kingdom
  • IELTS Required: Yes

Research position overview

This PhD is part of the EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award 2026/27 in Civil Engineering. It investigates climate-resilient biogas upgrading technologies to recover biohydrogen and biomethane from organic wastes.

Research Context

Anaerobic digestion of organic wastes produces biogas, which can be upgraded to renewable fuels. However, climate change may affect feedstock availability and process stability. Resilient upgrade pathways are needed.

What You Will Do

You will study various upgrading technologies (e.g., membrane separation, pressure swing adsorption) and assess their performance under different climate scenarios, considering economic and environmental factors.

Key Research Aims

  • Evaluate the technical and economic feasibility of different biogas upgrade routes.
  • Model the resilience of these processes to climate-related changes.
  • Propose optimal strategies for biohydrogen and biomethane production from organic wastes.

Supervisor Profile

Supervisor not named; refer to the School of Civil Engineering website for details.

Eligibility Requirements

  • Academic Background: First-class or 2:1 Honours degree in civil engineering, environmental engineering, or a related field.
  • English Language: IELTS required.
  • Nationality: UK only.

Funding Details

  • Funding Type: EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award.
  • Stipend: £21,805 per year.
  • Duration: 3.5 years.
  • Fees: Full academic fees covered.

How to Apply

Apply online via the University of Leeds PhD application portal.
